name: NBOC-DMT
effects: presumed DMT-class if Boc cleavage occurs

mechanismOfAction.summary: N1-Boc thermolabile prodrug of DMT; inactive until pyrolysis (~150–200 °C) or acid conditions cleave the Boc group, releasing DMT (5-HT2A agonist, σ1 ligand).
mechanismOfAction.description: 'NB-' prefix denotes N1-tert-butoxycarbonyl (NOT N-benzyl). The intact molecule is not itself active; the Boc group must be cleaved (pyrolysis/smoking or acid) to release DMT. Oral administration is inactive with or without an MAOI, because any absorbed intact compound must still be cleaved to DMT — claimed oral activity is unvalidated. Because the Boc-protected form is unscheduled, it is a common legal precursor form of DMT. No pharmacokinetic study or validated human dosing for the Boc compound.
